name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.159.0 — /spec:doctor check 20 becomes Expiry readiness and gains a second derivation: coverage-scope.js names each host file that parses acceptance-criterion ids beside a done status yet never mentions SHALL CONTINUE TO. Such a check demands a carrier for every criterion of a done spec, contradicts close-time test expiry, and deadlocks every close once the close deletes those tests — the remedy is to scope its carriers to specs that are not done, per the grounding contract's § Test expiry. The scan runs whether or not the tree holds retirable tests, because the deadlock is a property of the gate rather than of today's retirable count; it is a conformance probe for hosts initialized before the contract carried that section, not a recurrence-earned guard, and it can be deleted once no readable host reports a finding across a full major version. 7.158.0 — Host gates must exempt done specs from per-AC test coverage, and a close-time red gate says so. The grounding contract gains a required § Test expiry: a check requiring a test carrier per acceptance criterion scopes its carriers to specs that are not done, because close deletes a spec's own tests and then re-runs the gate over that tree — a host check demanding a carrier for every AC of a done spec deadlocks every close, and relabelling criteria SHALL CONTINUE TO is never the remedy. /spec:init's architecture profiling now checks for such a coverage check while it reads what CI enforces, and the review driver's close-time gate and suite refusals name how many tests expiry just deleted, pointing at the contract section rather than leaving a session to restore the tests it correctly retired. 7.157.0 — The mocks seed derives its own records instead of asking for the client's. design/mocks/records/<entity>.json is a plain JSON array of at least three record objects, derived by the session from the seed's Product and Facts, the research brief and anything under design/mocks/references/; the {provenance: real|synthetic, records: [...]} wrapper and every check on where the data came from are gone, and an object wrapping the records is refused so there is one shape to derive and one refusal to read. Mock data is invented by definition, so no refusal sends the session to a human for it: the SEED step and every records remedy now say derive, never ask. The journey-drawn check that screens must carry the seed's values is unchanged.
